detailed_checks.topic: Every non-exempt detected F5 failure reaches kernel-owned bounded FAIL
detailed_checks.evidence: Traced run admission refusal; absent/disabled map; preparation failure; install_f5 post-publication discrepancy; original verify; extension install; gate install/readback; writable static checks; final seal/extension verify; missing scenario row; and assembly launch range/entry rechecks. Every ordinary detected refusal diverges through f5_unsupported, or directly f5_fail_report after first bridge latch claim. install_policy::<true> now returns false on the cpu_readback/task-gate-install/verify disjunction and the immediately enclosing short-circuit run condition invokes f5_unsupported. A clear latch yields f5_fail_report -> status2 -> fixed kernel FAIL literal -> report -> terminal. No user-controlled string, pointer, outcome or expectation is used. Shared preparation close_failure publishes terminal and returns false to the wrapper, not to boot.
detailed_checks.exemptions: The explicit once-latch nested refusal and inherited architectural #DF task mechanism are separate, not missing first-failure reports. This is not a promise that a fault which prevents exception delivery or a pre-gate hardware fault has a functioning F5 report.

detailed_checks.topic: Required STATE publication and exact nested caveat
detailed_checks.evidence: Both first PASS and first FAIL reach f5_report, which writes byte3 to retained STATE before UART. The corrected installer-failure branch no longer terminates with PREPARING through f3_install_terminal. The state store is an assembly x86 byte store consistent with inherited Release-store rationale, not a new generic ordering dispatcher. Preparation close_failure can publish STATE3 earlier; it is idempotently republished by the reporter.
detailed_checks.nested_interpretation: An event arriving after the first XCHG and before f5_report can win a nested handler that sees latch1 and jumps directly to f5_terminal. STATE may therefore remain PREPARING or SEALED, and an outer status1 may have been written without complete output. Section4 explicitly mandates nested halt without another report or decode. Section6 includes this edge and excludes arbitrary recursion/storm survival. This supplement does not invent an unconditional nested STATE-store requirement or waive missing normal-first-report publication. Host evidence must reject incomplete output/record/state; HLT or status1 alone cannot count PASS.
detailed_checks.df_interpretation: Section6 explicitly retains unchanged F3 emergency handling; #DF never counts F5 PASS and need not write the F5 record/STATE/literal. No #DF exemption applies to the nonarchitectural software installer discrepancy.

detailed_checks.topic: No silent software bypass or failure-to-success continuation
detailed_checks.evidence: Confirmed no F5 caller uses gdt_tss::install or gdt_tss::fail. The only production gdt_tss::install_f5 caller is run. A false return is a transport result inside a ! entry, not recoverable failure. It immediately selects f5_unsupported before any extension/seal/IRETD continuation. First unsupported vectors21/29/30 normalize kernel segments then call f5_unsupported without decoding a CPU tail. All bridge scalar guard failures jump to the fixed FAIL reporter. Other origin/shape failures fail before tail reads. Only latch refusal goes straight to halt by the explicit nested rule. F5 normalizer call fallthrough is a defensive CLI/HLT loop after a declared nonreturning bridge, not a feasible ordinary report bypass; exact emitted reachability remains pending.

detailed_checks.topic: No introduced panic, mutex, allocation, shared serial or formatting in corrected failure transport
detailed_checks.evidence: The correction adds two constant-policy wrappers and one bool branch/return, no owned object, destructor, heap call, lock acquisition, formatting or serial call. After the installer returns false, the transport consists of the run branch, naked f5_unsupported, XCHG, status store, fixed literal setup, STATE byte store and inline bounded COM1 loop. No call, indirect edge, allocator or panic symbol occurs in those assembly bodies. Existing cpu_readback/verify paths include mapping snapshots/locks and are preparation validation, unchanged by this split; they are not newly claimed panic-free emitted closures.
detailed_checks.boundary: No production or fixture ELF inspected. This is not strict emitted all-arms approval; generic Rust helper code can retain infeasible panic edges. Full exact-ELF multi-root/fallthrough/stack audit remains mandatory.
